groundburst.gui.scram: SCRAM: drop every control rod in at once

groundburst.holo_projector.tooltip: Hold near an unfinished multiblock to project it. Use to step through its layers.
groundburst.info.anthrax_residue: Where a toxin SCUD comes down, its toxin wells up out of the crater as a heavy green cloud and spreads over the ground as glowing anthrax residue. The residue poisons whatever walks through it and dries out over about eight minutes. A hazmat suit keeps it out.
groundburst.info.arms_dealer: The GLA's factory for Toxin SCUDs: an adobe compound (9x7, walls of Adobe Wall two high, the controller in the middle of the front wall) round a yard of Launch Pad, its workshop at the back. Load its parts and power it: it builds by itself, laying each SCUD out on its trestles.
groundburst.info.battery: Holds 50,000 FE. Charge it in the Battery Charger; later gear (Geiger counter, guns) runs on it.
groundburst.info.battery_charger: Charges a battery (or any other mod's chargeable item) at up to 512 FE a tick from the power its cables bring, then moves it to the output slot.
groundburst.info.canning_machine: Fills canisters and empties them again. Put an empty canister (liquids) or gas canister (gases) in and it takes 1,000 mB from the supply tank (left) to fill it; put a filled canister in and its 1,000 mB is poured into the catch tank (right). Pipes and buckets fill the supply tank; pipes, buckets and auto-eject drain the catch tank.
groundburst.info.capacitor_bank: Stores power: 100,000 / 1,000,000 / 10,000,000 FE, moving 1,024 / 8,192 / 32,768 FE a tick. Every face takes power in except the front, which pushes it out (turn it with the Wrench). It keeps its charge when picked up, and a comparator reads how full it is. The Creative Capacitor Bank (creative menu only) is always full and pushes up to 1,000,000 FE a tick.
groundburst.info.chemical_plant: Chemical Plant (2x2x2): put the controller down, then add an Energy Port beside it, a Fluid Port behind it, an Item Port in the far corner of that bottom layer, and four Reactor Glass on top. Right-click the controller, or hold a Holo-Projector, to see where each block goes (sneak-right-click opens it before it is finished). The controller itself connects to nothing: power goes into the Energy Port, items in and out through the Item Port, and fluids in and out through the Fluid Port (a Water Pump supplies water). Right-click with a bucket or canister to pour it in, sneak-right-click with an empty one to draw off the product.
groundburst.info.circuit_fabricator: Makes basic, advanced, military and quantum circuits, sensor arrays and superconducting coils. Coils need liquid nitrogen: pipe it into the coolant tank from a Cryogenic Condenser, or pour in a canister.
groundburst.info.clean_room: Clean Room (3 wide, 2 deep, 2 high): put the controller down, a Clean Room Panel to its right and an Energy Port beyond that; behind them a Fluid Port, an Item Port and a panel; on top, three Reactor Glass across the front and behind them two Fan Filter Units and a panel. A Holo-Projector shows where each goes. Power goes into the Energy Port, wafers, phosphorus, packages and exotic matter in (and chips out) through the Item Port, photoresist, hydrofluoric acid, trichlorosilane and argon through the Fluid Port.
groundburst.info.creative_fluid_tank: Creative only. Pour a bucket or canister of any fluid in and the tank holds an endless supply of it: buckets, canisters and pipes can draw from it forever. Pouring in a different fluid switches it over; sneak-right-click with an empty hand to clear it.
groundburst.info.cruise_engine: A missile assembled with a Cruise Engine (Light and Medium missiles) is a cruise missile, winged and painted as its warhead's own: a booster lights it out of its box, then its jet carries it 40 blocks over the ground, following the ground's rise and fall, for up to 1,500 blocks; short of the target it pops up and dives on it. Only the Cruise Missile Launcher fires it.
groundburst.info.cruise_launcher: Fires cruise missiles, and only those. Build a 2x6 deck of Launch Pad with the controller and an Energy Port side by side in its front row, an Item Port behind the Energy Port and two Launch Boxes on its back row; keep the space over the deck clear where its boxes lie and rise (the Holo-Projector shows it). Load two cruise missiles (by hand, or by pipe or hopper into the Item Port) and power it (60,000 FE a missile); a Launch Computer aims, arms and fires it. Its rams raise the boxes during a 10 s countdown, then the two missiles go 3 s apart at the same target, each bursting its box's cover.
groundburst.info.decontamination_shower: A walk-in booth: pipe water in and power it, then step inside. It sprays whoever stands in it (20 FE and 10 mB of water a tick), putting out fire and washing off poison, wither and nausea. Radiation contamination will wash off too once radiation exists.
groundburst.info.die: Goes in the Industrial Press die slot and picks what the press makes. Dies are never used up.
groundburst.info.diesel_generator: Burns liquid fuel piped into its tank (or poured in from a canister) for 180 FE a tick: synthetic fuel gives 90 FE per mB, liquid rocket fuel 140; other mods' diesel works too. It pushes power out of its energy faces and pauses when its buffer is full.
groundburst.info.dosimeter: Carried anywhere in your inventory, the Dosimeter Badge keeps the dose you have taken: its film darkens from white through yellow, orange and red to black, and the dose shows in rad under the Geiger reading. Sickness starts at 100 rad and grows worse at 200, 400 and 600; 1,000 rad is lethal. The dose falls by itself, 1 rad a minute, below 10 RAD/h; Rad-Away and the Anti-Rad Injector take it down faster, and the film clears with it.
groundburst.info.exotic_matter_fabricato: Holds exotic matter in a spinning magnetic cage to make stabilised exotic matter, containment cells and singularity seeds. It draws 400 FE a tick, more than copper cable carries: feed it with insulated or high-voltage cable.
groundburst.info.fallout_ash: A nuclear burst on the ground, a dirty warhead or a reactor meltdown sends a plume of debris off on the wind: it lays radiation along its path and Fallout Ash on the ground, a layer at a time. The ash is weakly radioactive; shovel it away (it drops nothing), or leave it to weather into plain Ash over a couple of hours.
groundburst.info.fission_reactor: Fission Reactor (any size from 3x3x3 to 6x6x6): a hollow box with Lead-Lined Casing on its corners and edges, and casing or Reactor Glass on its faces, with exactly one Item Port, one Fluid Port and one Energy Port among them; the controller goes in a wall or the bottom edge of its wall. Inside it, every Fuel Channel holds one uranium fuel rod, wherever it stands (up to 64 in a 4x4x4 core); the rest of the core is left empty for the coolant. Right-click the controller or hold a Holo-Projector to see its plan as ghost blocks: the size set with the PLAN buttons on its screen (sneak-right-click to open it). Formed, its walls become one vessel with a control-rod drive over every column of channels. The controller connects to nothing: pipe coolant into the Fluid Port, feed rods through the Item Port and take power from the Energy Port. Every loaded rod gives 75 FE a tick with the control rods out (4,800 from sixty-four) and they all burn at once, each lasting about 2 hours 40 minutes at full power, a little more or less. Heat goes by how full the core is: with water coolant, past about 70% rods out it climbs past 900 C and goes critical (SCRAM it, or it melts down at 1,400 C); heavy water (Chemical Plant: deuterium and liquid oxygen) keeps it below that even at full power and lasts five times longer. Without coolant the core heats up fast; water left between the channels makes it heat and cool more slowly. Target rods in the breeding slots come out irradiated: DU rods for plutonium, lithium-6 rods for tritium (reprocess them in the Chemical Plant).
groundburst.info.fluid_pipe: Fluid pipes carry what machines push out of faces with auto-eject and fluids switched on, and what pipe sides set to Pull (with the Wrench) draw out of tanks and machines, sharing it between every tank on the run's normal sides. Pipes hold nothing themselves, so breaking one never spills. A run carries as much as its weakest pipe: copper 150, steel 600, pressurized 2,400 mB per tick.
groundburst.info.fluid_tank: Each Fluid Tank holds 16,000 mB. Touching tanks join into one when together they fill a box with a square base up to 3x3 and up to 5 high (720,000 mB). Fluid only moves in and out by pipe: pipes fill it from any side, and a pipe set to pull (with the Wrench) empties it.
groundburst.info.fluids: Chemical fluids live in machine tanks, pipes, canisters and (liquids only) buckets. Spilled acids burn, napalm ignites and liquid oxygen or nitrogen freeze anything standing in them.
groundburst.info.frozen_ground: A cryo burst freezes the ground it reaches: rime on stone and grass, plants frozen solid, and ice crystals grown round its middle. Where snow would not lie it thaws again over the next quarter of an hour or so; in cold places it stays. Frozen plants and crystals melt away (silk touch keeps a crystal).
groundburst.info.fusion_fuel_synthesizer: Presses lithium-6 dust with deuterium gas (piped in from an Electrolytic Separator) into lithium deuteride pellets, the fuel of thermonuclear weapons.
groundburst.info.fusion_reactor: Fusion Reactor (9x9x3 octagonal ring, the Particle Accelerator's footprint): a base ring of machine casing with the controller at the front centre, a Fluid Port in the middle of the right side and an Energy Port at the back; a ring of toroidal field coils above it with reactor glass viewports in the middle of each side; a ring of vacuum vessel casing on top; and a central solenoid column three blocks tall in the middle. Pipe deuterium, tritium and liquid nitrogen into the Fluid Port. To light the plasma it needs an ignition charge of 2,000,000 FE through its Energy Port (a big capacitor bank); once lit it makes 6,000 FE a tick and pushes it out of the same port. Liquid nitrogen keeps its magnets cold (2 mB a tick): if the nitrogen or the fuel runs out the plasma goes out and must be lit again.
groundburst.info.gas_centrifuge: Pipe uranium hexafluoride gas from the Chemical Plant into the Gas Centrifuge to get enriched uranium nuggets and depleted uranium dust. Cascade: centrifuges joined flange to flange (the pipe flanges on their sides meeting, all facing the same way or the opposite way) run 15% faster for every other centrifuge in the line, counting up to 8 (+105%). The screen shows the cascade size.
groundburst.info.geiger_counter: Held in either hand, the Geiger Counter clicks faster the stronger the radiation where you stand and shows its meter in a corner of the screen (a needle from 0.1 to 10,000 RAD/h, and the reading); anywhere in the hotbar it clicks and shows the reading alone. Sneak and use it to set its alarm (1, 10, 100 or 1,000 RAD/h, or off). It runs on its own charge, 5 FE a second while on: charge it in a Battery Charger. An EMP knocks it out.
groundburst.info.item_pipe: Item pipes carry items between inventories. A pipe side set to Pull (with the Wrench) draws items out of the chest or machine it touches (a machine only gives from its outputs); machines with auto-eject, and hoppers, can push in too. The run hands everything straight to the inventories on its other sides, shared in turn, never back where it came from. Pipes hold nothing, so breaking one never drops items. A run moves as many items as its weakest pipe: iron 8, steel 32, pneumatic 128 items a second (a hopper moves 2.5).
groundburst.info.lead_container: Radioactive items you carry dose you as surely as a crater does: a stack of uranium ingots brings sickness within half an hour, a spent fuel rod within three minutes. Nothing inside a Lead Container reaches you. It holds nine stacks of radioactive items and nothing else; use it to open it.
groundburst.info.membrane: Goes in the Cryogenic Condenser's membrane slot and picks what it draws from the air: liquid oxygen, liquid nitrogen or argon. Membranes and sieves are never used up.
groundburst.info.nuclear_missile: China's superweapon, an above-ground coffin. Build its hall (5 wide, 15 long, walls of Fieldstone Wall two high, the controller in the middle of the front wall) on a floor of Launch Pad with the Missile Erector at the back, its 3x3 control house beside the front and a Gantry Frame tower nine high beside the back (the Holo-Projector shows it). Load a Nuclear Missile and power it: it charges for 6 minutes, then a Launch Computer aims, arms and fires it. The roof opens, the missile is raised and it climbs straight out: a nuclear blast and a radiation field 200 blocks round.
groundburst.info.particle_accelerator: Particle Accelerator (9x9 octagonal ring, two layers): an octagon one block wide, three blocks straight on each side with a five-block staircase at each corner. Bottom layer Steel Plating; top layer Accelerator Magnet Segments with the controller at the front centre, the Injector beside it, the Target Chamber at the back centre, an Energy Port in the middle of one side and an Item Port in the middle of the other. Right-click the controller or hold a Holo-Projector to see where each block goes. It fills a containment cell with antimatter at 2,000 FE a tick. The controller itself connects to nothing: feed power into the Energy Port (insulated cable carries 1,024 FE a tick per run) and containment cells into the Item Port, which also gives out the antimatter cells.
groundburst.info.proton_exchange_membran: Goes in the Electrolytic Separator's membrane slot: with it, the separator splits water for hydrogen (its oxygen is vented); with the slot empty, it concentrates deuterium instead. Never used up.
groundburst.info.radiation_medicine: Potassium Iodide halves the dose you take for 10 minutes: take it before going in. Rad-Away draws 150 rad out over 30 seconds. The Anti-Rad Injector takes 400 rad off at once, but leaves you weak for a minute.
groundburst.info.rtg: A steady 40 FE a tick from a radioisotope slug. An enriched uranium ingot lasts two in-game days (plutonium, from the Fission Reactor, will last ten). The slug decays whether the power is used or not, so wire it to something that always draws.
groundburst.info.salvage: Found in the shafts of abandoned missile silos and among the wreckage of crashed missiles: a broken nuclear warhead. It is weakly radioactive (keep it in a Lead Container). A Chemical Plant leaches its core out with sulfuric acid: enriched uranium, often plutonium, and the steel of its case.
groundburst.info.scorched_ground: What a nuclear blast leaves of the land: the fireball burns earth, stone, sand and wood to scorched and glassed ground and charred trunks, leaves ash where the fires burned, and melts the crater's wall to slag, trinitite and irradiated soil (both radioactive). Strong radiation kills plants: dead leaves drop away, crops wither, and dead grass grows back once the ground is safe again.
groundburst.info.scud_storm: The GLA's superweapon. Build it on a 15x15 pad of Launch Pad with its controller in the middle of the front edge, a 3x3 Toxin Tank two high in the middle, nine SCUD Erectors round it and an L of Adobe Wall (two high, a watchtower four high at each end) down its left side and across its back (the Holo-Projector shows it). Load up to nine Toxin SCUDs and power it: it charges for 5 minutes, then a Launch Computer aims, arms and fires it. The erectors raise the SCUDs and they go one after another, coming down within 16 blocks of the target: heavy blasts, toxin clouds and anthrax residue spreading over the ground.
groundburst.info.sides: Every machine has a side-configuration tab (the wrench on the right of its screen): choose which faces accept items, give out products and connect to power, and switch on auto-eject. Multiblock structures have no tab: they connect only through their Item, Fluid and Energy Ports.
groundburst.info.singularity_reactor: Singularity Reactor (5x5x5): a machine casing floor and roof, steel plating posts at the corners, reactor glass walls, a containment emitter in the middle of each wall and of the roof, and a core cradle floating in the centre of the empty chamber. The controller is in the middle of the front of the floor, an Item Port on the left and an Energy Port on the right; any other floor block can be swapped for an extra Item Port to feed it faster. Put a singularity seed in the controller (it stays there, like a battery in the charger) and charge the cage with 500,000 FE through the Energy Port: the cage engages and holds the seed. Then it eats the items in its feed slots, any item at all. Every item is worth 10,000 FE and it eats at most 20 items a second, so its output is set by how fast you feed it: 10 items a second gives 5,000 FE a tick, 20 a second gives the full 10,000. Holding the cage costs 1,000 FE a tick, the worth of 2 items a second, and it keeps a 500,000 FE reserve for that. Take the seed out to shut it down safely. If the cage runs out of power, or the structure is broken while it holds the seed, the singularity collapses and the seed is destroyed.
groundburst.info.toxic_soil: Where a heavy anthrax cloud lies on the ground, or a toxin SCUD's residue settles, the soil turns. Toxic Soil kills what grows on it, breathes a thin anthrax haze now and then, and is spent (coarse dirt) after about a day.
groundburst.info.vertical_launch_battery: Ripples a volley of up to sixteen Light or Medium missiles onto one area. Its cells are six blocks deep: dig a pit four by four and five deep and fill it with Missile Canisters; on top of them, level with the ground, sixteen Strike Cells four by four with the air over them clear; in front of the cells a walkway of four Launch Pads with the controller second from the left, and behind them Machine Casing, an Energy Port, an Item Port and Machine Casing (the Holo-Projector shows it). Load a missile into each cell (by hand, or by pipe or hopper into the Item Port; conventional warheads only, no cruise missiles) and power it (20,000 FE a missile); set its spread on its screen. A Launch Computer, the Launch Control Station or a Laser Designator aims, arms and fires it: after a 10 s countdown its cells fire one after another, a quarter of a second apart, each missile lighting in its cell and climbing out through its hatch to its own point of the spread round the target.
groundburst.info.war_factory: China's factory for Nuclear Missiles (9x13): an octagonal hall and a furnace annex of Fieldstone Wall, a missile yard of Launch Pad with a Crane Rail along it. Load its parts and power it: it builds by itself, its gantry crane laying each missile out on its cradles.
groundburst.info.waste_drum: Drums of nuclear waste, stacked in the rooms of old waste storage caves under bags of magnesium oxide. Each is radioactive; a stack of them reads high. Broken open, it gives its waste.
groundburst.info.wasteland: A nuclear blast leaves a wasteland over its scorched ground: the Nuclear Wasteland biome, grey-brown, its water a dead olive, ash drifting down and no animals. A crater fills with water where the land would flood it: next to the sea, a lake or a river, or deep below sea level where the ground is wet.
groundburst.info.water_pump: Place on a water source block and power it: it draws 50 mB of water a tick (the source is never used up) and pushes it out of its two side outlets into pipes, tanks and machines.
groundburst.info.wrench: Right-click a side of a fluid pipe to cycle it: Normal (fluid travels both ways), Pull (draws fluid out of the tank or machine it touches; shown by a striped collar), Disconnected. Right-click a cable side to connect or disconnect it. Right-click a machine to turn it. Sneak-right-click a pipe, cable, machine, tank or structure block to pick it up.
groundburst.interceptor.tip2: Climbs at 100 blocks a second; bursts beside its missile
groundburst.interceptor_complex.incomple: Finish building it first (the Holo-Projector shows what is missing)
groundburst.jei.any_fuze: Impact or Barometric: where it hits, or in the air over the target
groundburst.jei.info.alarms: Alarm devices talk over alarm channels (0 to 9999; right-click a device to set its channel and choices). A channel goes off while any of its senders has something wrong: a Missile Warning Receiver sees a missile a working Radar Array tracks coming down within its warning radius; an Alarm Panel is switched on, or powered by redstone; a Hazard Monitor reads radiation over its threshold, or poison gas. Then every Air-Raid Siren, Klaxon and Alarm Bell on the channel sounds, every Warning Beacon and Emergency Light lights, every Alert Display shows what is wrong and every Alarm Relay gives redstone. Any of them also goes off when powered by redstone itself. The receiver, the monitor and the relay give redstone out. None needs power.
groundburst.jei.info.interceptor_battery: The Interceptor Battery shoots down missiles coming down near it. Load Interceptor Missiles into it (by hand or by pipe): its four cells fill from its store, one every three seconds. Powered, it watches the sky: a missile bound for within 256 blocks of it, if a working Radar Array tracks it, or 96 on its own seeker, draws an interceptor, two for class L and bigger missiles. Each kills its missile 80%% of the time against a small one, less against bigger ones (48%% a Strategic missile, 40%% an intercontinental one), against those coming down fast from high up, and a superweapon's; without radar, six tenths as often. A missile shot down breaks up in the air, its warhead never going off. Missiles flying out from near it, bound elsewhere, it lets go. An EMP knocks it out, and fries interceptors flying through one.
groundburst.jei.info.interceptor_complex: The Interceptor Complex is the multiblock missile defence: two and a half times an Interceptor Battery's reach, surer interceptors and bigger volleys. Build a 5x5 deck three high: the controller in the middle of a front row of Launch Pad; behind it six Launch Cells, three across and two deep, a Launch Pad either side and the space over them clear; at the back a deckhouse of Machine Casing two deep and three high, six Phased Array Panels in the middle of its front over the deck, and the Energy and Item Ports low in its back wall (the Holo-Projector shows it all). Its 24 cells fill from its store, one a second. Powered, it engages missiles coming down within 640 blocks of it that a working Radar Array tracks, or 240 its own radar sees: two interceptors at each, four at class L and bigger, fired two at a time; its radar guides them all the way in, so each kills a small missile 95%% of the time (less against bigger ones, those coming down fast and a superweapon's), radar or not. If they all miss and there is time, it fires again. It shoots down any missile coming down within its reach, yours too: switch it off with redstone while you fire close by. An EMP knocks it out.
groundburst.jei.info.laser_designator: Hold use to lase: a red beam and spot as far off as you can see, seen by everyone, zoomed in your sight with the range and coordinates. Use it on a Launch Control Station to join its network; it commands the network's launchers loaded with laser-guided missiles (a Laser Guidance Unit), one at a time: the first, or scroll while zoomed to pick the next. Left-click while lasing: an unarmed launcher is aimed at the spot and armed; an armed one launches, and its missile follows your laser in, wherever you point it; sneak and left-click to disarm it. Zoomed, armed launchers' targets show as spheres. 40,000 FE (100 s of lasing); charge it in a Battery Charger. Smoke breaks the beam; an EMP knocks it out.
groundburst.jei.info.launch_control_stat: The Launch Control Station runs your launchers anywhere in the dimension, loaded or not. Build it 3 wide, 2 deep and 3 high: a front row of Machine Casing with the controller in the middle (the desk); behind it Machine Casing two high with the Energy Port in the middle of the bottom row (the instrument bank); an Antenna on top of the bank's middle. Take Launch Codes from it (use them on the station), then use them on each launcher's controller or any part of it (Launch Silo, Launch Complex, Missile Silo, Cruise Missile Launcher, SCUD Storm, Nuclear Missile) and on Radar Arrays to link them; sneak to unlink. Its map shows the whole dimension: pick launchers, aim them (several take a pattern), ARM and LAUNCH, at once or timed so they all land together. Unloaded launchers are woken to launch; they need their energy stored. 40 FE/t.
groundburst.jei.info.upgrade_chips: Upgrade chips go in the Upgrades tab on the left of a processing machine's or an assembler's screen: three slots, and the chips in them add up. A speed chip makes it work 10%% faster a circuit tier (40%% at quantum); an efficiency chip makes it use 5%% less power a tier (20%% at quantum); a balanced chip does half of each. Two balanced chips are made from a speed and an efficiency chip.

groundburst.missile.accuracy_blocks: Lands within %s blocks of the target
groundburst.missile.accuracy_laser: Homes on a laser spot, else within 4%
groundburst.missile.cruise_tip: Makes a cruise missile: low over the ground all the way; fires from a Cruise Missile Launcher
groundburst.missile.hardened_tip: Optional: an EMP never leaves the missile a dud
groundburst.missile.strategic_tip: Takes nuclear warheads only; fires from a Launch Complex or a Missile Silo
groundburst.missile.tip.cruise: Cruise missile: flies low over the ground; fires from a Cruise Missile Launcher
groundburst.missile.tip.empty: Assemble one at an Ordnance Assembly Bench
groundburst.missile.tip.exotic: Exotic: fires from a Launch Complex or a Missile Silo
